questions.stem: In 1990, for the first time, Michaele Blease and W. French Andresco of the National Institute of Health, Bethesda, U.S.A. attempted gene therapy on a human patient. Which of the following disease was attempted to be cured?
questions.solutionHtml:
Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease
  • The first convincing therapeutic effect from gene transfer occurred with: SCID

Important types of defects in SCID

  • X-linked Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease (SCID):
    • mutations in the gene (IL2RG).
    • IL2RG encodes γc subunit of cytokine receptors.
    • Inheritance pattern: X-Linked.
  • The most common cause of SCID is IL2R defect.
  • Autosomal Recessive SCID:
    • ADA (Adenosine Deaminase enzyme) deficiency.
    • Gene therapy is done for ADA deficiency SCID.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 662

questions.stem: Change in the number of trinucleotide sequence repeats is involved in giving rise to certain disorders. All of the following diseases are due to an excessive number of glutamine residues (trinucleotide CAG repeat extension) in proteins, EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
Myotonic dystrophy
  • Myotonic dystrophy is due to ↑ CTG repeat, not CAG
  • Codon CAG codes for glutamine (Q)

Poly Q disorders

  • Those diseases which are due to CAG repeat e.g.
    • Spinobulbar muscular atrophy (Kennedy disease)
    • Spinocerebellar ataxia
    • Huntington’s disease.

Other Disorders:

Disease

Repeat

Fragile X syndrome

CGG

Friedreich’s Ataxia

GAA

questions.stem: The ring in the nitrogenous bases of DNA has a system of conjugated double bonds hence absorbing UV light like aromatic amino acids. This is a very valuable tool to measure DNA/RNA concentration in purified nucleic acids samples using UV spectrophotometry. Nucleic acids as a whole absorb UV light maximally at the wavelength of:
questions.solutionHtml:
260nm

Nucleic acids absorb UV light maximally at the wavelength of 260 nm

  • 260/280 ratio of pure DNA/RNA is in the range of 1.8 to 2.
  • Amino acids absorb UV light (not visible light) → colorless.
  • Aromatic amino acids absorb UV light at 250-290 nm (maximum absorption is at 280 nm) because of conjugated double bonds.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 331

questions.stem: Analysis of one strand of a double-stranded piece of DNA displayed 25 mol % A, 20 mol % T, 35 mol % G, and 20 mol % C. Which one of the following accurately represents the composition of the complementary strand?

options.label: A
options.text: [A] is 25 mol %, [T] is 20 mol %, [G] is 35 mol %, and [C] is 20 mol %.

options.label: B
options.text: [A] is 20 mol %, [T] is 25 mol %, [G] is 20 mol %, and [C] is 35 mol %.

options.label: C
options.text: [U] is 20 mol %, [T] is 25 mol %, [G] is 20 mol %, and [C] is 35 mol %.

options.label: D
options.text: The composition of the complementary strand cannot be determined from the data given.

questions.answerText: [A] is 20 mol %, [T] is 25 mol %, [G] is 20 mol %, and [C] is 35 mol %.
questions.solutionHtml:
[A] is 20 mol %, [T] is 25 mol %, [G] is 20 mol %, and [C] is 35 mol %.
  • In a double-stranded DNA, Chargaff's rule is followed
  • That is the base pairs in double-stranded DNA require that [A] = [T], and [C] = [G].
  • Therefore, if the concentration of A in one strand is 25 mol %, the concentration of T in the complementary strand must also be 25 mol %.

Hence the base composition of the complementary strand is:

In given strand

In complementary strand

A = 25

T = 25

T = 20

A = 20

G= 35

C= 35

C= 20

G = 20

Note: Chargaff’s rule is not applicable for RNA and ssDNA




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 349

questions.stem: The process of gene regulation involves the folding and unfolding of tightly packed DNA. This occurs by binding a variety of proteins and enzymes at the DNA surface through charge-charge interactions. At physiologic pH, the charge present in DNA is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Negative charge

Nucleic acid carries a negative charge at physiological pH

  • The negative charge at physiologic pH is due to the presence of the Phosphate backbone which provides a uniform negative charge on the outside.
  • This property is useful for the separation of DNA or RNA by electrophoresis.
  • DNA will move toward the anode. Shorter DNA molecules will move faster than longer molecules in agarose gel electrophoresis and get separated.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 349

questions.stem: Nucleosomes are a fundamental unit of DNA organization. It consists of histones complexed to DNA. Histone proteins present in nucleosomes are rich in which of the following amino acids?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lysine and Arginine

Histone proteins:

  • Rich in positively charged amino acids, lysine, and arginine.
  • Carboxyl terminal 2/3rd of histone molecules are hydrophobic.
  • Amino-terminals 1/3rd are particularly rich in basic amino acids. This amino-terminal end protrudes out of the octamer and is known as the histone tail.
  • Amino acids of histone tail undergo post-translational modifications.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 361

questions.stem: About nucleotides in DNA, all the following are correct, EXCEPT:

options.label: A
options.text: The nucleotide is formed by a combination of purine/pyrimidine base, sugar, and phosphoric acid.

options.label: B
options.text: The 3′ hydroxyl of one sugar is linked to the 5′ hydroxyl of another sugar through a phosphate group.

options.label: C
options.text: Nucleotides are linked by 3′ to 5′ phosphodiester bonds to form long polynucleotide chains

questions.solutionHtml:
None of the above

All the above statements are true.

  • Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) is composed of 4 types of deoxyribonucleotides, i.e.
    • Deoxyadenylate (AMP)
    • Deoxyguanylate (GMP)
    • Deoxycytidylate (CMP)
    • Deoxythymidylate (TMP)
  • The nucleotide is formed by a combination of base + sugar + phosphoric acid.
  • These units are linked by 3′ to 5′ phosphodiester bonds to form long polynucleotide chains
  • The 3′-hydroxyl of one sugar is linked to the 5′-hydroxyl of another sugar through a phosphate group




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 348-349

questions.stem: Several techniques such as PCR, in situ hybridization, RFLP, etc. require DNA strands to be separated for analysis. Heating is one of the most common methods to denature a dsDNA into single-stranded form. At a widely used temperature in molecular biology technique called Tm or melting temperature, what percentage of dsDNA is denatured?
questions.solutionHtml:
50%

Melting temperature or Tm

  • The temperature when half (50%) of the helical structure is denatured.
  • At lower temperature, the melted strands are re-associated; this is called annealing.
  • When DNA is denatured, unstacking of bases occurs resulting in increased absorbance at 260 nm. This phenomenon is known as hyperchromicity.


Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 351

questions.stem: If one strand of DNA contains the sequence “ATCGCGTAACATGGATTCGG”, what will be the sequence of the complementary strand using the standard convention?
questions.solutionHtml:
CCGAATCCATGTTACGCGAT
  • DNA and RNA are directional molecules. They are always written in the sequence of 5’ to 3’.
  • Phosphodiester bonds link the 3′- and 5′-carbons of adjacent monomers. Each end of a nucleotide polymer thus is distinct.
  • We, therefore, refer to the “5′-end” or the “3′-end” of a polynucleotide, the 5′-end being that with a free or phosphorylated 5′-hydroxyl group.
  • DNA sequences are complementary and antiparallel to each other.
  • If one strand of DNA contains the sequence “ 5' ATCGCGTAACATGGATTCGG 3' ” the sequence of the complementary strand will be 5' CCGAATCCATGTTACGCGAT 3'

Note: In the question or answer option if nothing is mentioned about the direction of the sequence, you have to automatically assume that they are asking in a 5'-3' direction as it is an internationally accepted convention.





Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 335

questions.stem: Restriction endonucleases also known as molecular scissors are enzymes widely used in molecular biology techniques such as gene cloning, recombinant DNA technology, RFLP, etc. These enzymes cleave:
questions.solutionHtml:
Double-stranded DNA

Restriction endonuclease

  • Cleaves double-stranded DNA at palindromic sites/ restriction sites
  • A palindromic sequence is a sequence in which both strands read the same when read in a 5’ to 3’ direction as shown below:

5' → AAGCTT - 3'
3' → TTCGAA - 5'

  • RE are Found in bacteria
  • They can create sticky ends or blunt ends




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 445

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true EXCEPT:

options.label: A
options.text: Heterochromatin is the relatively uncondensed portion of DNA.

options.label: B
options.text: Euchromatin represents the transcriptionally active portions of the DNA.

options.label: C
options.text: Histones are positively charged because of the high content of basic amino acids in them.

options.label: D
options.text: Methylation of DNA will increase the condensed portions

questions.answerText: Heterochromatin is the relatively uncondensed portion of DNA.
questions.solutionHtml:
Heterochromatin is the relatively uncondensed portion of DNA.

Heterochromatin

  • Condensed DNA (not uncondensed)
  • Tightly bound DNA which is transcriptionally inactive

Euchromatin

  • Uncondensed
  • Loose DNA, which is transcriptionally active.

Histones

  • Rich in basic amino acidse. arginine and lysine (positive charge).
  • Highly conserved proteins across organisms.

Methylation of DNA

  • Leads to gene inactivation or heterochromatin formation.
  • Mostly occurs at cytosine residue in DNA.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 361-363

questions.stem: Understanding the structure of DNA, and the process of replication, made us develop various drugs that interfere with DNA replication in pathogens. The type of bond seen between the phosphate group and 5’ carbon of ribose sugar within a nucleotide is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ester bond
  • The question asks about the bond in a single nucleotide and not between two nucleotides. Hence the answer will be an ester bond and not a phosphodiester bond.
  • Ester bond or Phosphoester bond >> Acid Anhydride

Bond between 2 nucleotides

Phosphodiester bond

Bond between Phosphate & sugar with a nucleotide

Ester or phosphoester bond

  • The bond between 5’ or 3' carbon of sugar & Oxygen anion of phosphate is an ester bond (phosphoester or acid anhydride bond).
  • Beta N-glycosidic bond is between N-base & sugar.
  • Between two nucleotides, this phosphate group will form two C-O links (one with 5’ C of incoming sugar & other with 3’ carbon of the previous sugar), so it is known as a 3’5’ phosphodiester bond.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 349

questions.stem: The diseases occurring due to mutation in the mitochondrial genome are called mitochondrial disorders. These disorders mainly affect the brain and CNS due to defects in ETC and aerobic respiration. All of the following are mitochondrial disorders EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
Incontinentia pigmenti

Mitochondrial DNA disorders

MELAS– Mitochondrial Encephalopathy, Lactic Acidosis, and Stroke-like episodes

Leigh syndrome

Leber hereditary optic neuropathy

Kearns Sayre syndrome

NARP syndrome – Neuropathy, Ataxia & Retinitis Pigmentosa

MERRF - Myoclonic epilepsy with ragged-red fibers

Incontinentia pigmenti (Bloch-Sulzberger syndrome)

  • Skin, hair, teeth & CNS manifestations



Robbins Basics of Pathology 9th Edition Page No. 171

questions.stem: Turner syndrome is a genetic disorder with a monosomy of the sex chromosome and genotype XO. In this disease, only females are affected. False about Turner’s syndrome are all except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Normal intelligence
  • The question is asking about the true statement about Turner's syndrome out of all options. Only Normal intelligence is true and while all other options provide a false explanation of Turner's syndrome as explained below:

Turner syndrome

  • Genotype is XO
  • Female is affected
  • Only monosomy compatible with life
  • Have zero Barr bodies (A normal female has one Barr body)
  • Intelligence is normal

 





Textbook of Pediatrics, Nelson, 20th Edition, Page Number: 2744

questions.stem: True statement(s) among the following about inheritance of an X-linked recessive trait is/are:50% of boys of carrier mothers are affectedTransmitted through affected femalesMales are occasionally affectedMost common sex-linked pattern100% incidence of affected sons from an affected motherSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1, 4, and 5 are correct

X-linked Recessive (XR) inheritance

  • Most common sex-linked pattern
  • Males are usually affected
  • Transmitted through unaffected females
  • In X- Linked inheritance, there is no male-to-male transmission.
  • In the X-linked recessive trait, 50% of boys of carrier mothers are affected (Fig 1.)
  • 100% incidence of affected sons from an affected mother suggests XR inheritance (Fig 2.)

Fig 1- Inheritance from carrier mother

Fig 2- Inheritance from affected mother






Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 142

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy has short stature, coarse facies, stiffening of the joints, and mental retardation. His parents, a 7-year-old brother, and a 9-year-old sister, all are unaffected. Mother had a family history of a disease with similar progressive symptoms in one of her brothers who died at 16 years of age and in one of her nephews (her sister’s son). The patient’s mother is pregnant. The risk of the fetus having the same disease is:
questions.solutionHtml:
25%
  • The patient’s normal parents (unaffected father and carrier mother), one normal sister (normal daughter), and normal brother (normal son) again indicate an X-linked recessive inheritance according to the chart below.
  • As the pedigree chart of the mother’s family shows no presence of disease in the mother (normal daughter .) but in one brother (affected son in fig.) and in the nephew from his sister (son of carrier daughter in fig.), it again confirms an X-linked recessive inheritance pattern.
  • Coarse facial features is a typical feature of Mucopolysaccharidosis (MPS) and Hunter syndrome has an X-linked recessive pattern.
  • Given X-linked recessive inheritance, the mother must have the abnormal allele on one of her X chromosomes (she is a carrier) in order for her son and brother to be affected. Her fetus has a 1/2 chance of being a boy and a 1/2 chance of being affected given male sex, resulting in a 1/4 (25%) overall risk of being affected.



Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No.

questions.stem: If both parents have sickle cell anemia, then the likelihood of children (offsprings) having the disease is:
questions.solutionHtml:
100%

Sickle cell anemia

  • Inherited as AR.
  • If both parents are affected, means both parents are homozygous for the trait as the recessive allele is expressed in only the homozygous state.
  • Then 100 % offspring will inherit the disease.
  • If Both parents are carriers then only 25% will be affected





Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 141

questions.stem: Which of the following statements are true/false about DNA?Two strands are held together by peptide bondsNon-covalent bonds in the sugar-phosphate backboneThe most common DNA is Z- DNAThe melting point of DNA is closely related to the Cytosine + Guanine content of DNAThe distance spanned by one turn of B-DNA is 3.4nmSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1-F, 2-F, 3-F, 4-T, 5-T

DNA Structural features:

  • 2 strands are held together by hydrogen bonds.
  • There are covalent bonds (3’-5’ phosphodiester bonds) in the sugar-phosphate backbone.
  • The most common DNA is B-DNA.
  • The melting point of DNA is closely related to the Cytosine Guanine content of DNA as C and G have three bonds, as compared to the two bonds present between A and T.
  • A single turn of B-DNA about the long axis of the molecule contains 10 bp.
  • The distance spanned by one turn of B-DNA is 3.4 nm (34 Aº).
  • The width (helical diameter) of the double helix in B-DNA is 2 nm (20Aº).




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 350, 351

questions.stem: In a family, the mother is normal while the father has a genetic disease. All their daughters are carriers and sons are normal, what is the pattern of inheritance of disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
X-linked recessive (XR)

In XR inheritance:

  • The most common sex-linked pattern of inheritance (out of XD, XR & Y- linked inheritance)
  • X- linked genes usually code for enzymes
  • Males are usually affected
  • Transmitted through unaffected females

Here, there is no male-to-male transmission





Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 611

questions.stem: One gene one protein theory states that one gene can give rise to one protein. Following is/are exceptions to one gene one protein theory:
questions.solutionHtml:
Both a & b

20,000 genes in humans give rise to a total of 2.5 lakh proteins. Which cannot be explained by this theory. This can be explained because there are processes such as

RNA editing: Apo B48 & Apo B100 are synthesized from the same mRNA due to differences in RNA Editing/Chemical modification of RNA/Differential RNA Processing

  • In the liver, apo B mRNA is 100% translated to produce apoB100
  • In the intestine, the same apo B mRNA is acted upon by the cytosine deaminase enzyme which converts one of the cytosine bases (in the mRNA) to uracil converting the codon CAA to UAA (stop codon).
  • Later during translation of this mRNA protein synthesis gets prematurely terminated with the final protein missing some of the amino acids of apo B100 protein.
  • This short version of the protein is apoB48. Which lacks the hepatic receptor-binding domain (missing amino acids).
  • It has different properties than apoB100.
  • Alternate splicing: Multiple RNA forms can be generated from the same gene transcript by alternate splicing which gives rise to different proteins.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 402

questions.stem: In which of the inheritance, if the father is affected no offspring is affected, but if the mother is affected, all offspring are affected?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mitochondrial

Mitochondrial Inheritance

  • Mitochondria is derived only from the mother
  • Mitochondrial disease has a high incidence as:
  • Mitochondrial DNA repair cannot occur
  • Introns are not present
  • Continuous exposure to the oxygen free radicals
  • Therefore, have more chances of mutations in mitochondrial DNA

Mitochondrial Inheritance

Affected mother will transmit the disease to all offspring

X linked disease

No male-to-male transmission

Y linked disease

Affected father will transmit the disease to all son

Autosomal disease

Equal frequency of these disease in male and female




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 369

questions.stem: A 28-year-old patient visited a physician with complaints of increasing fatigue and muscle aches during exercise. He recalls avoiding sports activities in his younger years because he was not able to keep up. Stress testing reveals normal cardiac function, but blood tests show gradually increasing levels of serum lactic acid and ammonia under resting conditions. His physician suspects a mitochondrial DNA disorder that affects mitochondrial function due to mutation in mitochondrial genes. Which of the following options gives the names of mitochondrial pathways affected in this patient and also lists the compound linking these pathways?Glycogenolysis, glycolysis, and glucose 6-PCitric acid cycle, electron transport chain, and α-ketoglutarateCitric acid cycle and urea cycle, and fumarateGlycogen synthesis, gluconeogenesis, and malateCitric acid and urea cycle, and arginineSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1, 2, and 5 are correct
  • Mutation in the mitochondrial genome mainly affects oxidative phosphorylation leading to low ATP and anaerobic glycolysis with lactic acid accumulation, especially under stressful conditions such as exercise due to depletion of blood oxygen saturation.
  • A vicious cycle of exercise intolerance leading to muscle inactivity with fewer mitochondria exacerbates myopathy (muscle weakness and incoordination) in mitochondrial disorders.
  • All the reactions of the citric acid cycle and some of the initial reactions of the urea cycle are located primarily in the mitochondria, whereas glycogen and glucose metabolism pathways primarily occur in the cytosol (Options A and D are excluded).
  • α-keto glutarate and fumarate are intermediates of the citric acid cycle, but only fumarate is an intermediate of both the citric acid and urea cycles (Option B is excluded).
  • Fumarate and arginine are produced from argininosuccinate in the urea cycle, after which arginine is converted to ornithine to yield urea (option E is excluded) and fumarate is converted to malate and then oxaloacetate in the citric acid cycle.




Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry 6th Edition Page No. 707
